name: Burden of Proof
shortDef: Making a claim and demanding that others disprove it instead of supporting it.
definition: Putting forward a claim and then insisting that doubters prove it false, instead of giving evidence for it. Whoever makes a claim owes the reasons; skeptics don't have to disprove it first.
howToSpot: Who made the claim, and have they offered any evidence for it?
Is the speaker asking critics to disprove something they never supported?
Does doubting the claim get treated as if it were a rival claim needing proof?
classicExample: My lucky socks help the team win. If you think they don't, prove it.
legitimateVersion: Asking critics for counter-evidence is fair once you've already supported your claim, or when the critic is making a claim of their own, like asserting a well-tested product is dangerous.

contrast.fal_appeal_to_ignorance: Burden of proof hands the job of proving to critics; appeal to ignorance concludes a claim is true (or false) because it hasn't been disproven.
contrast.fal_moving_the_goalposts: Burden of proof dodges supporting a claim at all; moving the goalposts raises the bar after evidence has been provided.
